text:
ella: Quick sync: UX review notes for onboarding variants in staging. Keeping short bullets.

nate: dropping the link to the Figma branch: https://www.figma.com/file/staging/onboard-variants (frames: inline-helper, full-modal, mini-pill).

ravi: Main UX tradeoff: inline helper keeps context but is easy to miss; full-modal forces attention but is disruptive. We should A/B test completion rate vs. time-to-first-token.

soph: Accessibility first: modal must trap focus and restore it after close. For the inline helper, ensure aria-live="polite" announcements when the helper expands so screen reader users notice it.

ella: Copy variants I like: modal header = "Set up your first project" (direct), inline helper headline = "Quickstart: get a project running" (less modal-y). Also shortened CTA options: "Create project" vs "See examples".

nate: On sample projects list in the modal, can we add a small tag under titles: "example", "template", "full-stack demo"? That helps signal completion level. Also add a keyboard shortcut hint: Press "." to open quickstart later.

ravi: Implementation detail: persist progress in localStorage + server flag. If user starts but abandons, we show a subtle "Resume setup" entry in the Help menu for 14 days. If explicit Skip pressed, persist user.onboarding_skipped = true server-side.

soph: A11y nit: contrast on the inline helper footer link is borderline (3.7:1). Recommend swapping to a darker gray or reversing to white-on-accent and testing with axe. Also make sure link targets are at least 44x44 touch size on mobile.

ella: Measurement plan: track events onboarding.variant_viewed, onboarding.started, onboarding.completed, onboarding.sample_selected with properties { variant, sample_id, time_to_first_request }. We'll run the experiment for 2 weeks or until N=250 starts per variant.

nate: For the experiment, feature flag onboarding_v2 with rollout: 50% control (no helper), 25% inline-helper, 25% full-modal. Canary it on beta orgs first.

ravi: Dev question: should the inline helper auto-expand on first visit, or remain collapsed with a pulsing affordance? I lean collapsed to avoid layout shift; expand after 3s if user is idle.

soph: Keyboard behaviour: when collapsed, pressing Tab should land on the expand button before skipping to other header controls. Also provide skip link as first-focusable item inside modal.

notif-bot: staging deploy: onboard-variants/20223 deployed to https://staging.redwood.dev — visual changes live.

ella: Decision summary: run A/B as proposed; inline helper should default collapsed with optional auto-expand; modal traps focus; persist skip server-side; add tags to samples; fix contrast on footer link. I'll update the ticket and add acceptance criteria. Thanks everyone!
